prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign SAGITTARIUS: a bow and arrow seen from the front, like a crest: the bow lies level across the middle, its two limbs curving up in a wide symmetrical arc, the string drawn down into a V; one long straight arrow stands exactly upright through the centre, its broad head pointing straight up, its feathered end at the bottom. A single small four-pointed star shines just above the arrowhead.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, straight streaks of sparks and small shooting stars, long and short in turn, spread outward past the frame on all sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. Never fierce or scary. There is no face and no figure at all: only the object. The sign's nature shows only through form: one straight true line aimed high, a taut curve at full draw, open space ahead: freedom, honesty, optimism, the far horizon.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: ivory, flame orange, magenta red, deep indigo blue. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
